list.title: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis:
list.snippet: Leishmania major primarily causes cutaneous leishmaniasis, which is the most common form of the disease.

list.title: Skin Sores:
list.snippet: The infection leads to the development of skin sores or ulcers, often with a raised border.

list.title: Scarring:
list.snippet: These sores can heal, but they often leave permanent scars.

list.title: Transmission:
list.snippet: The parasite is transmitted to humans and animals through the bite of infected sand flies.

list.title: Other Names:
list.snippet: In various parts of the world, cutaneous leishmaniasis caused by L. major is known by different names, including Aleppo boil, Baghdad boil, Delhi boil, and others.

text_blocks.snippet: Leishmania donovani is a species of parasite that causes visceral leishmaniasis, also known as kala-azar, the most severe form of leishmaniasis. It's a vector-borne disease transmitted by sandflies and affects the internal organs, particularly the spleen and liver. If left untreated, it can be fatal.
snippet_highlighted_words: a species of parasite that causes visceral leishmaniasis, also known as kala-azar, the most severe form of leishmaniasis

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of Leishmania donovani and visceral leishmaniasis:

list.title: Transmission:
list.snippet: Leishmania donovani parasites are transmitted to humans through the bite of infected female sandflies.

list.title: Geographic Distribution:
list.snippet: It is prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions, including parts of Africa, Asia (especially the Indian subcontinent), and South America.

list.title: Pathology:
list.snippet: L. donovani primarily affects the mononuclear phagocyte system, including macrophages in the spleen, liver, and bone marrow.

list.title: Clinical Manifestations:
list.snippet: Visceral leishmaniasis is characterized by fever, splenomegaly (enlarged spleen), hepatomegaly (enlarged liver), anemia, and weight loss.

list.title: Complications:
list.snippet: Untreated visceral leishmaniasis can lead to severe anemia, immunosuppression, and potentially death.

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Diagnosis involves detecting parasites or parasite DNA in tissue samples, such as bone marrow or spleen aspirates, often through microscopy or molecular methods.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Treatment typically involves medication to kill the parasites, but prompt and complete treatment is crucial.

list.title: Post-Kala-azar Dermal Leishmaniasis (PKDL):
list.snippet: Some individuals who have been successfully treated for VL may develop PKDL, characterized by skin lesions with parasites.

list.title: Prevention:
list.snippet: Preventive measures include using insect repellent, mosquito nets, and controlling sandfly breeding sites.
